Title: Nepal raises flood missing toll by nearly 1,000 people to 6,150
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepal's disaster authority said Wednesday it had sharply revised up the number of people considered missing after the August 26 flood to 6,150, following data collection and verification in affected districts.
"We have been collecting details on the missing people from the district offices, and revised the data after verification," disaster authority spokeswoman Shanti Mahat told AFP.
The figure rose from 5,179 reported a day earlier.
The number of bodies retrieved stands at 1,403 bodies, 105 of which had been identified, according to the disaster agency.
Across the border in China, the toll is 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media.
The combined toll from the deadly glacial mountain collapse on the Nepal-China border from both nations now stands at 1,446 people dead and at least 6,669 missing.
Several hundred foreigners, including tourists and pilgrims, are among the missing.
The sheer scale of the flood was unlike anything witnesses had seen before, with the Nepali government pointing the finger at the dire impact of rising global temperatures on the Himalayan mountains.
Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people, contributes a fraction of global greenhouse gas emissions compared to industrialised nations.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah will take his first foreign trip as leader to address the UN General Assembly on the urgent issue next week.
Nepal estimates the reconstruction bill after the deadly floods will amount to $4.78 billion.

Title: Gaza apartment block collapse leaves 21 dead
Article:
GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: Gaza authorities said Wednesday that 21 people including five children had died after an apartment building collapsed from damage sustained in earlier Israeli strikes.
The six-storey building, which had four apartments per floor, crumbled overnight onto nearby homes and tents in the Tal al-Hawa area of Gaza City, according to the civil defence agency, which works as a rescue service under Hamas authority.
The vast majority of buildings in Gaza have been damaged or destroyed in Israeli strikes throughout the war with Hamas, according to the United Nations.
At Gaza City's Al-Shifa Hospital, AFP journalists saw weeping men carrying children's bodies wrapped in white shrouds.
Relatives crouched on the floor to say their final goodbyes to their loved ones, kissing the faces of the dead through sobs.
"These buildings are nothing but ticking time bombs," said Ahmed Al-Ajla, whose uncle and other relatives were killed in the collapse.
"Before his death, my uncle... had endured displacement, poverty, imprisonment and loss," Ajila told AFP.
"The war is not over, for there remain ticking time bombs in the form of houses on the verge of collapse."
The building, which was housing more than 100 displaced people, had sustained damage from previous Israeli strikes, the civil defence agency said.
It said its teams, "after hours of arduous work... recovered the bodies of 21 people who had been trapped under the rubble."
The civil defence said it had also helped transport 45 injured people to hospital.
In an earlier toll, civil defence agency spokesman Mahmoud Basal said that five children were among the dead.
The building was hit multiple times in 2024 and March 2025, leading to warnings for Gazans not to go back, Basal said.
"They have no other choice. With neither tents nor homes available, they are living in cracked, damaged buildings despite the risk of collapse," he added.
Earlier on Wednesday, AFP footage showed the building reduced to an immense pile of shattered concrete, towering over a team of rescuers in high-visibility vests conducting a desperate search.
Excavators bearing Egyptian flags worked to remove the debris, while rescuers and volunteers carried out the dead.
"My friend and neighbours live in this building. I came to help my friend retrieve some clothes and mattresses. He currently has no shelter or home," Mohannad al-Mashharawi told AFP.
The International Committee of the Red Cross said it had supplied materials to help the search effort at the request of local authorities.
Israel launched relentless strikes on Gaza after the Oct 7, 2023 attack led by Hamas that killed more than 1,200 people, the deadliest attack ever against Israel, according to Israeli official figures.
The ensuing Israeli military campaign has killed more than 73,700 people, according to Gaza's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
With so many Palestinians left homeless, and major shortages of construction materials, many Gaza residents have taken the risk of moving into the shaky buildings.
The UN's humanitarian coordinator for the occupied Palestinian territories, Ramiz Alakbarov, said he was "devastated" by Wednesday's news.
"Today's tragedy underscores the grave risks faced by families living in these structures and the urgent need for safer alternatives. No one should have to risk their life simply to find a safe place to shelter," he said.
Gaza's civil defence agency has identified around 2,000 buildings in the territory that it says are at risk of collapse.
Israel has allowed additional aid into Gaza since the declaration of a US-brokered ceasefire in October 2025.
But Israel has kept carrying out strikes and has restricted the entry of a range of equipment that it says could also have military use.

Title: Anwar: MA63 is a national promise, must not be seen as only affecting Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 17 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) is a national pledge or pact that must be respected and implemented, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said that MA63 is a solemn promise made by the previous leaders of Malaysia.
“We have made a promise. Our forefathers (leaders) decided to strengthen this bond (Malaysia). Therefore, we must take seriously the examination and review of all the decisions we made in the past.
“And I need to state that this issue (MA63) is unlikely to be resolved as long as some of our friends in the Peninsula believe that MA63 is only a matter for Sabah and Sarawak,” he said.
The Prime Minister said this while speaking at the national-level 2026 Malaysia Day Celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) here.
The guest of honour at the celebration was the Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
Commenting on MA63, Anwar said that nine issues related to the agreement have been resolved under the Madani Government.
He noted that among the matters resolved was the decision to recognise both Sabah and Sarawak’s Public Works Department (JKR) and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) as technical departments, as well as the appointment of permanent representatives from both states to the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
The Prime Minister also said that the Madani Government had also successfully handed over electricity regulatory powers to Sabah and transferred Bintulu Port to Sarawak.
“Resolving these matters requires good cooperation between the state governments and the federal government. If Sarawak prospers, it brings prosperity to Malaysia as well.
“So, when Bintulu Port belongs to Sarawak, it remains a vital port for Malaysia; I view it from that perspective — this is a pledge for Malaysia. It represents shared interests and shared wealth,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Armed Forces to add Cyber Force as fourth service by 2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is set to make history by establishing a Cyber Force as its fourth service by 2030, in a strategic move to confront evolving threats in the modern security landscape.
Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move was prompted by the fact that cyberspace and the electromagnetic domain have increasingly become arenas of competition and warfare on the global stage.
To this end, he said a dedicated team known as the Cyber Force Nucleus Team has been formed to spearhead planning, coordination, organisational transformation preparations, and capability development towards the force's official establishment.
He said the launch of the nucleus team is scheduled to be officiated by the Defence Minister in conjunction with the MAF Day Carnival 2026 at the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) Base in Lumut, Perak on September 19.
“We looked at models from other countries that have already incorporated this domain into their services. This is a very urgent need and we cannot afford to be left behind,” he said.
“This nucleus team will plan and explore how to turn the Cyber Force into a reality and have it fully operational based on the ministry's guidelines, to be realised by 2030,” he said in an exclusive interview for the 93rd MAF Day celebration.
Elaborating further, Malek Razak said in line with this aspiration, MAF is also continuously developing expertise in the field of Cyber and Electromagnetic Activities (CEMA).
He said cyber capabilities, electronic warfare and spectrum management operations have already been applied in practical terms to produce tangible operational effects through the
Exercise Camar Kilat
Series 2/26.
“This commitment is further strengthened through human capital, with 60 officers and 17 other ranks from the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) having attended CEMA-related courses as of July,” he said.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin had previously said the Defence Ministry is drawing up plans for a Cyber Force as its fourth service to tackle modern and cognitive warfare threats.
Mohamed Khaled said the move was driven by the fact that present-day threats are no longer confined to traditional physical combat, but are increasingly shifting towards the domination of cyberspace and public perception. — Bernama

Title: BUDI Diesel subsidy eligibility now transferable to non-family users, says Anwar
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 17 — The government has agreed to expand the BUDI Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) eligibility transfer facility, allowing registered owners of private diesel vehicles to transfer their eligibility to any eligible actual user, effective immediately.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said previously, the transfer of eligibility was restricted to immediate family members.
“Although we announced BUDI95 (BUDI Madani RON95) at 300 litres per month on the eve of National Day on August 31, pickup and jeep owners — an issue prevalent in Sabah and Sarawak — were still voicing their grievances, so we raised the subsidised diesel limit to 400 litres per month.
“But this is the meaning of democracy — we listen. There were still some concerns, and ministers from Sabah and Sarawak raised these concerns, so in addition to last month’s announcement, the government has agreed to improve BUDI Diesel,” he said at the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) here last night.
In addition, Anwar said registered owners of more than one private diesel vehicle were allowed to transfer the monthly BUDI Diesel eligibility of those vehicles to a maximum of three other vehicles.
According to the Prime Minister, the transfer of monthly eligibility under the BUDI Diesel initiative is subject to an appeal application.
The celebration, themed ‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’, was also attended by the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar. Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
Meanwhile, the Finance Ministry (MOF) said in a statement that approved recipients would receive their own monthly eligibility to purchase subsidised RON95, subsidised diesel, or a combination of both.
However, the transfer of eligibility does not involve any change in vehicle ownership.
“Registered owners can transfer their eligibility to any Malaysian citizen holding a valid MyKad who is eligible for BUDI95 and is the actual user of the designated vehicle.
“Once the application is approved, the recipient can use their MyKad to purchase subsidised diesel based on the diesel vehicle assigned to them,” the statement read.
MOF said registered owners with more than one private diesel vehicle could transfer the monthly eligibility of those vehicles to a maximum of three other individuals, subject to the total number of registered diesel vehicles.
At the same time, registered owners will retain the monthly eligibility for any private diesel vehicles that have not been transferred, for their own use.
“For example, if Mr Alias owns four private diesel vehicles, he can transfer the monthly eligibility of those vehicles to the actual users, such as his wife, child, and employee. Mr Alias and the three individuals will each receive their respective monthly eligibility based on the type of vehicle used.
“For eligible private diesel jeeps or pickup trucks, Mr Alias, as the registered owner, must apply for an additional 100 litres per month, subject to specified conditions, before an application to transfer eligibility can be made,” MOF added.
In situations where an owner transfers all three diesel vehicles owned, MOF said the registered owner will only be eligible for the BUDI95 subsidy.
“For each eligible vehicle, the transfer is only allowed once. Once approved, the eligibility cannot be transferred back to the registered owner or to another individual, except under specified special circumstances.
“A recipient can only receive an eligibility transfer from one registered owner,” the statement read.
Applications under the new rules can be made starting yesterday via the BUDI Madani portal at
www.budimadani.gov.my
, physically at Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) offices, or by seeking further information and assistance at nearby petrol stations.
To enable eligibility to be used starting the 1st of the following month, applications must be submitted by the 27th of the current month.
“For example, applications submitted by September 27 will be processed to allow eligibility to be used starting October 1, subject to data verification and validation.
“Eligibility transfers approved prior to September 16 remain final. Registered owners with more than one vehicle can still submit new applications, subject to the maximum limit of three transfer recipients and the total number of registered diesel vehicles,” MOF said.
All transfer applications still pending as of September 15 will be returned to applicants, and registered owners who still wish to transfer eligibility must submit a new application starting September 16 based on the new policy rules.
For further information, the public can contact the BUDI Madani Call Centre via telephone at 1300-88-9595, WhatsApp at 03-2631 4595, or email
tanya@budimadani.gov.my
. — Bernama

Title: DKU accuses Negeri Sembilan exco of treason, coup attempt against Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) has accused the Negri Sembilan state executive council of treason and attempting to overthrow Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
According to a letter issued by Messrs Halim & Ismail last night, sighted by Malay Mail the law firm said it was acting for the first and second defendants in Seremban High Court Originating Summons No. NA-24NCvC-240-05/2026, namely Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, the DKU secretary, and the DKU.
The letter was addressed to Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and copied to members of the state executive council, the state secretary and the state legal adviser.
It referred to the '
Kenyataan Media Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan — Keputusan Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri, Negeri Sembilan Bil 6 Tahun 2026'
dated Sept 15.
The solicitors said their clients noted that Ismail had relied on the April 19, 2026 proclamation for the purposes of the media statement.
They said the proclamation did not satisfy the mandatory conditions under Article 10 of the Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan 1959 and was therefore “null and void and of no legal effect”.
The letter also referred to the exco statement declaring that Tuanku Muhriz had been removed as Yang di-Pertuan Besar by the Undang Yang Empat, and that Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar had been selected and recognised as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar with immediate effect.
In response, the solicitors said their clients were “shocked by your reckless announcement”.
They said the exco did not have the jurisdiction, authority or power to make the announcement, which they described as unconstitutional, void and of no legal effect.
“It is our clients’ firm view that your conduct in issuing the abovementioned announcement is to subvert the executive authority of Tuanku Muhriz under the UUTKNS, and is further intended to overthrow and dethrone Tuanku Muhriz,” the letter said.
The solicitors further alleged that the conduct was “tantamount to a coup d’etat and an act of treason”, which they said should be punishable under the Penal Code and other relevant laws.
In its statement on Tuesday, the state exco said the April 19 proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz had been signed and sealed by the legitimate Undang, and that the decision to remove him was the absolute prerogative of the Undang Yang Empat, the four ruling chiefs who elect the state ruler.
It also said Ismail’s signature as menteri besar on August 3 completed the proclamation in accordance with the state constitution.
The statement, however, did not address the DKU’s position that Article 10 of the state constitution, which allows the four chieftains to remove a ruler, requires a thorough enquiry.
Ismail had previously claimed he was forced to sign the proclamation on August 3 and subsequently lodged a police report over the matter.

Title: Anwar, Abang Johari witness Bintulu Port handover to Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg yesterday witnessed the official handover of Bintulu Port to the Sarawak state government from the federal government, marking a new chapter in the management of the strategic port.
The handover was particularly significant as it took place as Sarawak hosted the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations yesterday.
At the handover ceremony held at the Kuching International Airport, Transport Minister Anthony Loke represented the federal government, while Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas represented the state government.
According to a statement by the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development, the handover involved four key documents, namely the Ports (Privatisation) (Amendment of Schedule) Order 2026 and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) (Vesting Date) Order 2026. Also handed over were documents relating to the determination of the effective date of the Declaration of an Area in the District of Bintulu to be a Federal Port (Repeal) Act 2024 [Act 858] and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act 2024 [Act 859].
“With the coming into force of Act 858 and Act 859 on September 1, Bintulu Port officially changed its status from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government,” the statement said.
The transition also saw the dissolution of the Bintulu Port Authority (LPB), with the port authority functions taken over by the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak), a state statutory body established under the Port Authorities Ordinance 1961.
The statement said that effective September 1, 2026, all assets, rights, interests and obligations of LPB were transferred and vested in the Sarawak government.
The takeover of Bintulu Port took about three years, beginning with Abang Johari’s announcement of the takeover intention on January 30, 2023, before the proposal was approved by the Sarawak Cabinet in February that year. The Prime Minister also announced the agreement to hand over Bintulu Port when tabling Budget 2024 in parliament on October 13, 2023.
The federal and state governments subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding on March 22, 2024, before the legislative process was finalised with the passage of Act 858 and Act 859 by the Dewan Rakyat in July 2024.
On February 4, the federal and Sarawak governments reached an agreement on the takeover value of LPB amounting to RM1.8 billion. A “completion agreement” was subsequently signed on June 21, 2026, followed by a cheque handover ceremony from the Sarawak Government to the federal government in Bintulu. — Bernama

Title: Former Negri Sembilan MB backs Tuanku Muhriz as lawmakers question exco statement on royal succession
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Former Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on the people of the state to stand behind Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, as two Pakatan Harapan lawmakers questioned whether a state executive council statement affirming his removal represents the official position of the state government.
Aminuddin, who is also Negri Sembilan PKR chief, called for solidarity with Tuanku Muhriz and urged the public to defend the institution of constitutional monarchy.
“I call on all the people of Negeri Sembilan to stand united and pray for the well-being of His Royal Highness Tunku Muhriz, as well as to defend the sovereignty of the institution of constitutional monarchy.
“Reject leaders who betray the royal institution and violate the (state) constitution. Our loyalty is only to the king and country,” he said in a Facebook statement today.
Bahau assemblyman Teo Kok Seong, a former state exco member, meanwhile questioned whether a joint statement by exco members could be regarded as the official position of the state government.
He said official government positions or announcements were usually issued through the menteri besar or the state secretary’s office.
“Therefore, a joint statement by the exco members only reflects the position of the exco members concerned and should not be regarded as the official position of the state government,” he was quoted saying by
Malaysiakini.
Nilai assemblyman and opposition leader J. Arul Kumar separately called for an immediate explanation over what he described as two different and seemingly contradictory statements concerning Tuanku Muhriz and the royal institution.
He was referring to a statement by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim yesterday and the exco statement issued yesterday.
Ismail had said the menteri besar did not have unilateral power to remove a sitting ruler and had invoked the state constitution.
Arul said exco members could express differing views during discussions but the government’s position should be unified once a decision had been reached.
“If it is true that there are two conflicting statements regarding the same matter, this situation must be clarified immediately by the state government,” he was quoted as saying.
He also called on the state government to explain the decision reached at the exco meeting, including whether both statements were based on the same decision and, if not, which was valid.
The latest reactions come amid a months-long dispute over the Negeri Sembilan throne.
In its statement yesterday, the state exco said the April 19 proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz had been signed and sealed by the legitimate Undang, and that the decision to remove him was the absolute prerogative of the Undang Yang Empat, the four ruling territorial chiefs who elect the state ruler.
It also said Ismail’s signature as menteri besar on August 3 completed the proclamation in accordance with the state constitution.
The statement, however, did not address the position of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), which said Article 10 of the state constitution, allowing the four chieftains to remove a ruler, requires a thorough enquiry.
Ismail had previously claimed he was forced to sign the proclamation on August 3 and lodged a police report over the matter.

Title: Anwar: RM500 domestic flight aid for new students travelling between peninsula and Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The government has announced a one-off RM500 special assistance for domestic flight ticket purchases for every eligible new student of public higher education institutions (IPTA) for the September or October intake this year.
“The intake for public universities, polytechnics and community colleges is in September and October. This will benefit 7,095 students who need to fly between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Sarawak, and the Federal Territory of Labuan to begin their studies,” said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He announced the aid during the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching last night.
He said the measure was part of the Federal Government's commitment to easing the people's burden, alongside announcements on improvements to the BUDI Madani Diesel initiative and restructuring of special grant entitlements for Sarawak.
Anwar had earlier announced that Sarawak's interim special grant would be increased to RM1.5 billion this year, up from RM600 million previously.
He said the Federal Government would continue engaging with the Sabah and Sarawak state governments to finalise a sustainable formula to determine the annual Special Grant rate. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s OPR stays at 2.75pc: What does it mean for your loans, savings and spendings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) has kept its Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent, maintaining the rate for a seventh consecutive meeting.
At 2.75 per cent, the OPR is now at its lowest since the Covid‑19 pandemic era, when it was cut to 1.75 per cent — a rate that remained in place until July 9, 2025, when it was raised back to 3 per cent.
With the OPR left unchanged at 2.75 per cent, the focus now shifts to what this means for borrowing costs, savings returns and day‑to‑day spending.
What does the OPR do
The OPR is Bank Negara’s key monetary policy rate.
It influences interest rates in the banking system, including rates for loans and deposits, although changes to the OPR do not necessarily translate one-for-one to every financial product.
Put simply, the OPR affects the cost of borrowing money and the returns on some forms of savings.
When the OPR is lowered, borrowing can become cheaper, which can support household and business spending and investment.
When it is raised, borrowing generally becomes more expensive, which can moderate demand in the economy.
How does Bank Negara decide the OPR?
The OPR is not calculated using a fixed formula.
Bank Negara’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) considers the outlook for inflation and economic growth, as well as risks to the economy, before deciding whether to raise, lower or maintain the rate.
It considers factors including economic growth, inflation, domestic demand, financial conditions and developments in the global economy.
Why did Bank Negara keep it at 2.75 per cent?
At its September 3 meeting, the MPC decided to maintain the OPR at 2.75 per cent.
Bank Negara said the current monetary policy stance was consistent with the outlook for continued price stability and sustainable economic growth.
Malaysia’s economy grew by 6 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation stood at 1.8 per cent in July, according to BNM.
BNM said the economy’s solid growth momentum was supported by stronger-than-expected export performance alongside sustained domestic demand.
It also said global growth remained resilient, supported by strong technology-sector expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labour markets.
Inflation measures how quickly the prices of goods and services are changing. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Why doesn’t Bank Negara simply set the OPR based on inflation?
This is because the two measure different things.
Inflation measures how quickly the prices of goods and services are changing.
The OPR is a policy interest rate used by Bank Negara to influence economic and financial conditions.
So an inflation rate of 1.8 per cent does not mean the OPR should also be 1.8 per cent.
Bank Negara considers inflation alongside economic growth and the risks facing the economy.
For borrowers with a floating-rate or variable-rate home loan, the interest rate can change over time rather than remaining fixed throughout the loan period. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
How does it affect a home loan?
This is where the OPR can have a more direct effect on households.
For borrowers with a floating-rate or variable-rate home loan, the interest rate can change over time rather than remaining fixed throughout the loan period.
For new retail floating-rate loans in Malaysia, the Standardised Base Rate (SBR) is linked solely to the OPR.
Banks then add a spread that reflects factors such as the borrower’s credit risk and the bank’s costs.
So if the OPR falls, the SBR falls and the interest rate on a loan linked to it can fall as well, and if the OPR rises, the reverse can happen.
The exact effect on your monthly instalment depends on the terms of your loan.
Are car loans affected?
One should not assume that a car instalment will automatically change when the OPR moves.
The effect depends on the type of financing and the terms of the agreement.
For individuals who are already carrying debt, interest rates matter because they determine how much it costs to borrow, and in the case of revolving credit card balances, how much interest can accumulate over time. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
What about credit cards and other debts
For individuals who are already carrying debt, interest rates matter because they determine how much it costs to borrow, and in the case of revolving credit card balances, how much interest can accumulate over time.
When interest rates rise, borrowers with loans or other credit facilities linked to variable rates may face higher repayment costs.
When rates fall, the cost can come down for those same types of borrowing.
However, the impact depends on the type of debt and the terms of the financing.
An unchanged OPR, therefore, does not mean every borrower’s monthly repayment will remain exactly the same, nor does a change in the OPR automatically affect every type of loan.
It affects savings accounts and fixed deposits
In this area, the OPR affects savers as well as borrowers.
Interest‑bearing deposits are accounts where a bank pays you a return for keeping your money with it.
Common examples include savings accounts and fixed deposits (FDs).
When interest rates are higher, banks may offer higher returns on some deposits, particularly FDs.
However, when rates fall, deposit rates may also decline.
The same broad principle applies to Islamic banking deposits, although their returns are structured differently from conventional interest.
However, deposit rates do not necessarily move by exactly the same amount as the OPR.
Banks also consider factors such as competition, funding requirements and their own pricing decisions.
BNM had said it would remain vigilant to developments affecting domestic inflation and growth, particularly given external risks such as geopolitical tensions and energy costs. — Picture by Firdaus Latif.
What are some takeaways from the decision?
For households, the simplest takeaway is that there is no new OPR change following the latest decision.
For borrowers with rates linked to the OPR, that means there is no new OPR-driven increase or decrease in borrowing costs from this decision.
For savers, deposit rates will continue to depend on individual banks and products rather than moving automatically with the OPR.
An unchanged OPR also does not mean prices will stay the same, as the OPR influences overall demand and financial conditions rather than directly controlling the prices of goods and services.
BNM had said it would remain vigilant to developments affecting domestic inflation and growth, particularly given external risks such as geopolitical tensions and energy costs.
For now, the OPR remains at 2.75 per cent, with the next scheduled MPC decision on November 5, 2026.

Title: Police confirm body found in Perak waters is missing angler
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 16 —Police have confirmed that the body of a man found floating in the waters off Hutan Melintang, Perak, this morning is one of the three anglers missing since Monday.
Klang Utara police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said the body was identified as Mohd Sharil Abd Rahman, 43, following identification by next-of-kin.
He said the search and rescue (SAR) team received information from fishermen about the discovery around 8.30 am before the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) brought the body to Hutan Melintang Jetty for further action.
“The body will subsequently be sent to Shah Alam Hospital for further procedures,” he said in a statement today.
Ramsay said the joint SAR operation to locate the two remaining missing victims is ongoing. It involves the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), MMEA, Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM), and other relevant agencies.
“Further updates regarding the operation will be communicated from time to time,” he said.
Earlier today, Klang Utara deputy police chief Supt Mohd Rahimi Zainol said the body, tied to a drum and wearing a life jacket, was spotted in the waters off Bagan Sungai Belukang, Perak.
He added that according to survivors, all victims tied themselves to drums after their boat capsized near One Fathom Bank in the Straits of Malacca on Monday.
Selangor MMEA launched the SAR operation at 3.35 am on Monday after receiving reports of seven missing anglers. Four were rescued safely in Sekinchan waters on Tuesday and sent for treatment at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR) and Banting Hospital.
The survivors were identified as Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43; Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali, 45; Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, 45; and boat skipper Zulfikalnain Awang, 47.
The two anglers still missing are Muhamad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamad, 49.

Title: Diesel, RON97 and unsubsidised RON95 prices up by RM0.35 for Sept 17-23 period
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 35 sen per litre for the Sept 17-23 period, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said.
In a statement today, MOF said the retail price of RON97 would increase to RM4.85 per litre from RM4.50, while unsubsidised RON95 would rise to RM4.37 from RM4.02 and unsubsidised diesel to RM5.27 from RM4.92.
The ministry said the increase in global fuel prices was driven by heightened tensions in West Asia amid the conflict, which has entered its 200th day.
“Iran had attacked 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for US attacks on five Iranian tankers, while attacks also extended to Yemen and Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure. Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen to single-digit levels following the surge in attacks.
“The situation worsened after drone attacks forced the temporary suspension of operations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which is among the key routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said.
MOF said these developments drove Brent crude oil prices back above US$100 per barrel, reaching nearly US$110 per barrel during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period.
At the same time, the ministry said disruptions to refining capacity in Russia and constraints on crude oil supplies continued to limit the production of refined petroleum products, keeping refining margins high and putting upward pressure on global petroleum prices.
According to MOF, escalating tensions in West Asia and the Russia-Ukraine conflict could result in prolonged volatility in global petroleum prices.
Meanwhile, MOF said the Madani Government would continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of global uncertainties, including by maintaining targeted BUDI Madani subsidies for eligible consumers.
Under BUDI95, eligible recipients will continue to pay RM1.99 per litre for RON95, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.38 per litre, or 54 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.37.
For BUDI Diesel, recipients will pay RM2.10 per litre, with the government providing a subsidy of RM3.17 per litre, or 60 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM5.27.
The basic monthly eligibility limit for BUDI95 and BUDI Diesel was raised again to 300 litres effective Sept 1, while eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps would receive an additional 100 litres, bringing their total monthly eligibility to 400 litres, the ministry said.
“The Madani Government will continue to take a prudent approach to protect the people from price fluctuations while ensuring the nation’s fuel supply remains sufficient and secure,” the statement read. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Malaysia supports and appreciates Saudi Arabia’s efforts following drone interception in Mecca
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia has expressed its support for Saudi Arabia following the successful interception of a drone near Mecca, asserting that any attempt to threaten the security and sanctity of Islam’s holiest city is completely unacceptable.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia appreciates the swift action taken to safeguard the safety of residents and pilgrims in Mecca.
“I have been following reports on a drone that was successfully intercepted near Makkah al-Mukarramah.
“This incident serves as a reminder of the need to avoid any actions that could further escalate tensions in the region,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar called for an immediate halt to all attacks on civilian areas and any actions that endanger the security and sanctity of holy sites.
He added that all parties involved must choose the path of peace through dialogue to de-escalate tensions and seek a resolution without delay. — Bernama

Title: Haze alert: 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia record unhealthy readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A total of 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollution Index (API) readings as of 5 pm today.
According to the API management system (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor - Johan Setia (183), Shah Alam (170), Petaling Jaya (164), Klang (160) as well as Banting and Kuala Selangor (159), two areas in Kuala Lumpur - Cheras (174) and Batu Muda (170), three areas in Negeri Sembilan - Nilai (170), Seremban (165) and Port Dickson (148), along with Putrajaya (170) - recorded API readings at the unhealthy level.
Areas in the northern region with unhealthy API readings include four in Penang - Minden (166), Balik Pulau (165), Seberang Jaya (160) and Seberang Perai (158), five in Perak - Seri Manjung (166), Tasek Ipoh (164) Tanjung Malim (161), Taiping (157) and Pegoh Ipoh (153), as well as two in Kedah - Sungai Petani (158) dan Kulim Hi-Tech (155).
On the East Coast, three areas in Terengganu recorded unhealthy API readings - Kuala Terengganu (162), Besut (145), Kemaman (141) and Paka (133), one in Kelantan -  Tanah Merah (155), and five areas in Pehang Temerloh (155), Jerantut (152), Indera Mahkota, Kuantan (143), Balok Baru and Kuantan (142).
Down south in Johor, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings - Tangkak (134), Kluang (124) and Batu Pahat (103), as well as three areas in Melaka - Bukit Rambai (155), Alor Gajah (153) and Bandaraya Melaka (145).
Also, 21 areas in the country had moderate API readings, including in Sarawak - Kuching (79), Samarahan (67), Sibu (66), IPD Serian (60), Bintulu (58), Mukah (53), Miri (52), and Sabah - Tawau (73), Kimanis (66) and Keningau (54).
API readings between zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (dangerous). — Bernama

Title: Selangor MB: Follow-up haze measures to be reviewed on Friday
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — The Selangor government will review follow-up measures to address the deteriorating haze situation, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the matter would be discussed in detail, based on reports from all relevant parties, at the Selangor State Executive Council meeting scheduled for Friday.
“This Friday we have an exco meeting. We will carefully discuss the follow-up measures, because after it (haze) cleared a bit on Sunday, the situation worsened again, especially yesterday and today. We will see on Friday according to reports from all parties,” he said.
He said this to reporters after officiating the Festival Turath Islami Malaysia 2026, at Masjid Putra here today, which was held in conjunction with the Festival Turath Islami Malaysia 2026.
Amirudin said the state government also needs to obtain information from the State Health Department and related agencies before determining the appropriate measures.
“Appropriate measures include trying to assist at school and supervising our children while they study. This is because they spend a considerable amount of time at school, and we need to limit outdoor activities to avoid exposure to the haze and similar conditions,” said Amirudin.
Six areas in Selangor recorded Air Pollution Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4.30 pm today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy levels, namely Johan Setia (183), Shah Alam (170), Petaling Jaya (164), Klang (160), and both Banting and Kuala Selangor (159).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100 (moderate); 101 to 200 (unhealthy); 201 to 300 (very unhealthy); and above 301 (hazardous). — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Day: PM Anwar calls for renewed commitment to unity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia Day serves as a reminder that the nation was built on a covenant between the government and the people, between the regions and the Federation, and between loyalty and justice, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In a Facebook post in conjunction with Malaysia Day today, he said Sept 16 represents a commitment that must constantly be renewed to ensure no region is marginalised, no community feels alienated, and no citizen is left behind in the country's progress.
However, Anwar said it should be acknowledged that there were times when the nation’s journey had deviated, such as when racial issues were exploited, regional gaps were allowed to widen, and differences were turned into dividing walls.
"The sea may separate us, but not our national aspirations and hopes. Happy Malaysia Day!" he said. — Bernama

Title: New-generation MyKad applications open tomorrow with enhanced security features
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has unveiled the new-generation MyKad with a redesigned appearance and enhanced security features.
The new card incorporates several security elements on both its front and back, including a Dynamic Security Hologram and transparent window on the front.
The back of the card features an Enforcement QR Code and a dual-interface chip as part of the security upgrades.
View this post on Instagram
The new MyKad will be available when applications open tomorrow, with Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail advising Malaysians not to rush to replace their existing cards to avoid congestion at NRD offices.
He said the new MyKad has about 50 additional security features, which will be introduced in phases.
Existing MyKad holders can continue using their car

Title: Woman killed, sister and motorcyclist seriously injured after lorry hits their stalled car in Nilai
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A woman was killed while her sister and a motorcyclist were seriously injured after a lorry crashed into their broken-down car at Kilometre 284.4 of the North-South Expressway northbound near Nilai this morning.
Berita Harian
reported that the incident occurred at about 9am, when the motorcyclist, who had stopped to help move the car, was also hit in the collision.
Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the district traffic complaints counter received information about the accident from the Nilai district police operations room at 9.01am.
“Initial investigations found that the accident is believed to have occurred when a Perodua Axia driven by a 32-year-old woman was travelling from Melaka towards Perak.
“When it arrived at the scene, the Perodua Axia was believed to have broken down and stopped in the second lane from the left,” he said in a statement.
Johari said a 22-year-old man riding a Honda RS 150 arrived at the scene and tried to help the woman move the vehicle.
“Not long after that, a lorry driven by a 24-year-old man arrived at the scene and is believed to have failed to notice both the car and the motorcyclist.
“The lorry is believed to have crashed into the rear of the Perodua Axia and the motorcyclist who was providing assistance,” he was quoted as saying.
He said the Axia driver suffered serious head and body injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer.
“The passenger of the Perodua Axia, a 39-year-old woman, and the motorcyclist were seriously injured and both received treatment at the red zone of Hospital Tuanku Jaafar here,” he said.

Title: Police: Body found in Perak waters, believed to be missing Perak angler
Article:
KLANG, Sept 16 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three missing anglers intensified today following the discovery of a body in the waters off Bagan Sungai Belukang, Perak, believed to be one of them.
Klang Utara deputy police chief Supt Mohd Rahimi Zainol said the body, which was found in the Bagan Sungai Belukang area in Bagan Datuk, was reported to have been tied to a drum and was wearing a life jacket when it was discovered at about 9.30am today.
“The body is understood to have been taken to hospital for identification to ascertain the identity,” he told reporters at the Sementa Jetty here today.
Mohd Rahimi said those who survived included Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43, Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali and Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, both 45, as well as boat skipper Zulfikalnain Awang, 47.
“The three anglers still missing are Muhamad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, 43, and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamad, 49,” he said.
Based on accounts from the survivors, Mohd Rahimi said all the victims had to tie themselves to drums due to severe dehydration after the boat they were travelling in capsized.
He said after the boat capsized, they held hands and formed a group of seven.
Earlier, Mohd Rahimi accompanied Selangor deputy police chief DCP Mohd Zaini Abu Hassan to inspect the on-scene command post (PKTK) before visiting the victims’ families around Sementa Jetty here.
Meanwhile, Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer Lt Mohd Syafiq Sazali said the third day of the SAR operation focused more on the waters along the Selangor-Perak border based on an updated SAR system simulation.
Last Monday, MMEA mobilised its assets at 3.40 am after receiving information about the anglers’ disappearance, before the SAR operation was officially activated at 5 am.
Four of them were found safe in the waters off Sekinchan on the second day of the SAR operation before being sent for further treatment at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR) and Banting Hospital. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to seek preventive measures, diplomatic cooperation over transboundary haze, says Zahid
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 16 — Malaysia prioritises long-term diplomatic cooperation and early preventive measures over seeking compensation from neighbouring countries in addressing the issue of transboundary haze, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee Chairman, said a prudent and structured diplomatic approach is the most effective way to address sensitive issues among Asean member states while ensuring optimal technical coordination.
“While seeking compensation does not necessarily imply definitive liability that must be borne by any specific country, taking preventive measures early would avoid the need to address such sensitive inter-state issues.
“Diplomatic measures must be pursued alongside technical efforts involving officials from neighbouring countries and Malaysian states,” he told a press conference after chairing the First National Disaster Management High-Level Committee (HLC) Meeting of 2026 at Wisma Bapa Malaysia here today.
He was responding to a question on whether Malaysia intended to raise the issue of losses suffered by the country, particularly in terms of the economy, health and tourism, as a result of transboundary haze with the Indonesian government.
Also present were Sarawak Deputy Premier and Chairman of the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, and Deputy Minister of Rural and Regional Development, Datuk Rubiah Wang.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid, who is also Minister of Rural and Regional Development, said the transboundary haze issue would be officially raised during his working visit to Jakarta from tomorrow until Sept 20 in conjunction with the Halal-20 Conference: 5th World Halal Summit 2026 (H20 Summit).
“That (the transboundary haze issue) is among the topics to be discussed with the Minister of Environment or the Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (in the Malaysian context).
“There are seven ministers who will be holding discussions with me, covering other areas such as the halal sector and so forth.
“A key topic I will discuss and coordinate with Bapak Gibran (Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka) is the haze problem,” he said.
Regarding assistance to neighbouring countries, Ahmad Zahid said the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) had been directed to stand ready to coordinate cloud seeding operations (OPA) and logistical support to help tackle forest and peatland fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, should an official request be received from the relevant authorities there.
Meanwhile, in a media statement issued following the meeting, Ahmad Zahid said the government is shifting towards an “anticipatory action” approach to address the threat of extreme hot and dry weather caused by Super El Niño.
The measures include hotspot monitoring, ensuring the readiness of firefighting assets, peatland management, enforcement against open burning and disseminating health information to the public.
“The Department of Minerals and Geoscience Malaysia (JMG) and the Department of Environment (DOE) have been asked to evaluate the use of tube wells as an alternative water source, including refurbishing existing infrastructure in high-risk areas,” he said.
According to the statement, the National Disaster Management Council (MPBN) had also approved a total allocation of RM5 million this year for OPA and related management, comprising RM2 million for Phase One, approved on June 2, and RM3 million for Phase Two, approved on Sept 2. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to review impact of electricity bill increase at special meeting tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A special meeting will be held tomorrow with the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), the Energy Commission (EC), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
The meeting will review immediate mitigation measures to reduce the impact of the electricity bill increase on affected households.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that upon his return from India and the Maldives, his attention remained focused on the people’s concerns regarding the recent increase in electricity bills.
“I have heard the complaints raised, and this matter needs to be given attention and addressed immediately.
“I would like to emphasise that the effort to target subsidies will continue to be maintained to protect the majority of the people,” he said in a statement here today.
Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said that around 80 per cent of domestic users who consume electricity not exceeding 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) per month remain protected and are not affected by the rate increase following the rise in fuel costs this year.
“However, the haze conditions and hotter weather recently have driven an increase in electricity consumption among some households, causing their monthly usage to exceed the 600 kWh threshold and thus subjecting them to the Automatic Fuel Cost Adjustment (AFA),” he said.
Therefore, the Madani government will continue to ensure that every step in targeting subsidies is implemented fairly and reasonably, with the interests and well-being of the people always being a priority, he added. — Bernama

Title: Policeman injured while chasing 4WD involved in Kluang cable theft case
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 16 — A policeman on a routine crime prevention round was injured after falling from his motorcycle during a high-speed chase in Kluang town in the pre-dawn hours today.
Kluang deputy police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said the incident is believed to have occurred at 5.54am when two policemen on motorcycles were chasing a Mitsubishi vehicle.
He said the suspect, believed to be involved in an earlier cable theft incident, had an uncut cable at the rear of the vehicle.
“Two policemen on motorcycles were despatched to investigate the incident and came across the suspect’s vehicle that fled the scene.
“During the pursuit, a policeman fell and sustained injuries,” he said in a statement today.
Nik Mohd Azmi was responding to a video posted on Threads showing two policemen chasing a red Mitsubishi pick-up truck in Kluang town.
He said police are actively tracking down the suspect and vehicle involved in the incident and urged those with any information to contact the nearest police station or the Kluang district police headquarters.
“The case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft and also Section 353 of the same Code for use of criminal force against a public servant in discharging their duties,” he said.

Title: Negeri Sembilan DOE ramps up enforcement as haze hits unhealthy levels
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 16 — The Negeri Sembilan Department of Environment (DOE) is stepping up ground-level monitoring, particularly on open burning activities, following worsening haze conditions in several districts in the state.
State DOE director Abdul Aziz Parmin said other sources being closely monitored included factories, quarries, motor vehicles, development projects, land clearing and any activities that could contribute to dust emissions and cause air pollution.
“The priority at the moment is to step up ground-level monitoring, particularly on open burning activities, without neglecting other sources that could contribute to dust or haze emissions,” he told Bernama when contacted here today.
He said the department had issued letters to all local authorities (PBTs) and District and Land Offices (PDT) throughout the state, urging them to step up enforcement against pollution sources.
Abdul Aziz said air quality in several areas in Negeri Sembilan was at an unhealthy level, with Nilai recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 172, Seremban (168) and Port Dickson (155) as of noon today.
He said all actions related to the haze situation would be referred to the National Haze Action Plan, while at the state level, the department would continuously update the State Disaster Management Committee on the situation.
On cloud seeding, Abdul Aziz said the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) would coordinate the matter at the federal level based on current API readings and as necessary. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh: My views on Najib’s pardon given honestly
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 —Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she had expressed her views on former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon application during the Pardons Board meeting on Sept 11, after reviewing the written opinion of the Attorney General.
Hannah, who is a member of the Pardons Board, said she had expressed her views honestly, guided by her conscience and in the national interest.
“I expressed my views honestly, guided by my conscience and in the country’s interest,” she said in a statement here today.
The statement was issued in response to remarks by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said regarding the deferment of Najib’s pardon application.
Hannah said she had expressed her views in her capacity as the minister responsible for the Federal Territories.
At the same time, she said that under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, the authority and final decision on the matter rest with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
“Certainly, in accordance with Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, the authority and final decision lie with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, including the decision to defer any ruling regarding Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon,” she said.
Yesterday, Azalina was reported as saying that any questions or clarifications regarding the deferment of Najib’s pardon application should be directed to Hannah.
She said although the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) came under her ministry, it merely served as the secretariat for the Pardons Board and she was not the minister responsible for the board.
On Sept 11, the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division, in a statement,  announced that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, consented to defer the decision on Najib’s pardon application to a future meeting of the Pardons Board. — Bernama

Title: Schools advised to stagger students seeking medical checks, says Perak health exco
Article:
IPOH, Sept 16 — The Perak government has advised schools to coordinate with District Health Offices and relevant health facilities before bringing large numbers of students for medical examinations following an outbreak.
The advice came after a boarding school in Ipoh brought 57 students with Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) to a nearby health clinic simultaneously, despite being advised to bring them in stages.
Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said bringing symptomatic students in stages would help prevent congestion at health facilities and reduce the risk of infection transmission.
“The affected boarding school has been advised not to bring large numbers of symptomatic students to health facilities at the same time if more cases are identified,” he said in a statement.
Sivanesan said the Perak Health Department, through the Kinta District Health Office (PKD Kinta), was managing an Influenza A cluster at a boarding secondary school in Ipoh, with control measures, screening and epidemiological investigations carried out immediately.
Following the incident, he said health authorities conducted clinical screening and assessments, epidemiological investigations, laboratory sampling and other prevention and control measures to contain the spread among the school community.
“On September 14 at 12.08pm, 57 symptomatic students were brought simultaneously by bus to a nearby health clinic without prior notification.
“Some of the students also did not bring identification documents, affecting the smooth management of patients at the clinic,” he said.
Sivanesan said an integrated PKD Kinta and clinic team was also deployed to the school at around 2pm the same day to conduct centralised health screening and assessments.
“The team comprised a medical officer, assistant medical officer, healthcare assistant, pharmacist, an infection prevention and control team member and three PKD Kinta surveillance unit members,” he added.
However, on September 15, the school reported another 27 symptomatic students.
“Although the school was advised to bring symptomatic students to health facilities in stages to avoid overcrowding at the clinic, the school informed authorities that it intended to transport the students using a school bus.
“The clinic then coordinated with the school to ensure the admission, screening and assessment process could be carried out in an orderly manner,” Sivanesan said.
He said a further 12 symptomatic students were identified, bringing the total number assessed that day to 39.
“The assessment was completed at 1pm, with all students reported to be in stable condition.
“A total of 61 students had undergone health screening and assessment. Of these, 46 were diagnosed with ILI, 14 with upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) and one with conjunctivitis,” he said.
“Nasopharyngeal swab samples were also taken from six students for laboratory testing, with the results being monitored by PKD Kinta to determine further action,” he added.
Sivanesan said PKD Kinta was continuing epidemiological investigations and monitoring new cases among the school community to identify transmission patterns, the number of cases, contacts and related risk factors.

Title: Lim Guan Eng: Umno no longer brings value to Penang government amid cooperation with Perikatan, PAS
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 16 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has questioned the continued presence of Umno in the Penang unity government, saying the party has “no more value” to the administration when it is simultaneously working with Perikatan Nasional (PN) and PAS.
Lim said Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow appeared more focused on criticising him than addressing Umno’s recent attacks on PH, creating what he described as an impression that Chow feared Umno might quit the state government.
He stressed that his earlier remarks were aimed at Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, whom he accused of lacking the courage to challenge Penang PH to remove Umno from the state government — as Zahid had done at the federal level — rather than at Chow.
“Instead of hitting back at Umno for working with the opposition PN, Chow chose to criticise me,” Lim said, adding that Penang PH leaders should not be afraid of offending “an extremist Umno” that he claimed had indulged in divisive rhetoric against non-Muslim minorities and shown little inclusivity toward non-Malays.
Lim also pointed to Umno’s boast that it contributed to the defeat of DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook in the Chenaah seat during the recent Negeri Sembilan election, arguing that DAP leaders had every right to rebut Umno’s allegations against PH and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said Chow may prefer DAP leaders to stay silent, but there was “no gag order” from Loke.
Lim urged Penang PH leaders to take a clear stand on whether Umno should remain in the state administration and convey that position to the coalition’s central leadership.
“Has PH or Chow no firm position after all the attacks by Umno in their recent General Assembly?” he asked.
He claimed Umno was holding on to its positions in the state executive council, the two city councils and state-linked companies because it knew it would have little political impact if it left. Even without Umno’s two assemblymen, Lim said, PH would still command a two‑thirds majority in the Penang legislative assembly.
Lim warned that retaining Umno could damage public perception of Penang PH’s leadership, arguing that the coalition must recognise that “the greatest enemy is the enemy within”.
“PH Penang leaders should wake up to the reality that there is no more value for Umno to remain in the Penang state government when Umno can work actively with PN and PAS from within,” he said.

Title: Raja Muda of Selangor, MACC chief commissioner discuss anti-corruption initiatives
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — Efforts to strengthen the fight against corruption were among the matters discussed by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman.
The MACC said the matter was discussed when Tengku Amir Shah granted an audience to Abd Halim at Istana Selangor, Bukit Kiara, last Monday.
In a statement today, the commission said Tengku Amir Shah was also briefed on its latest developments and ongoing initiatives, particularly those relating to anti-corruption efforts in Selangor.
Abd Halim expressed his appreciation to Tengku Amir Shah for granting the audience and taking the time to receive a briefing on the MACC’s role and latest developments.
“He (Abd Halim) also expressed his gratitude for the Raja Muda of Selangor’s support and concern for ongoing efforts to combat corruption and uphold transparent, principled and accountable governance,” the statement read.
The audience was held as part of Abd Halim’s official engagements following his appointment as MACC Chief Commissioner last May 13. — Bernama

Title: Perak exco: 46 students at Influenza A cluster school suffer flu-like illness
Article:
IPOH, Sept 16 — Forty-six students at a boarding school in Ipoh have been diagnosed with influenza-like illness (ILI) following an Influenza A cluster detected at the school, Perak Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman A. Sivanesan said.
He said the cases were identified after health officials screened and assessed 61 students with symptoms up to Sept 14, while 14 others were found to have upper respiratory tract infections and one had conjunctivitis.
“As of Sept 15, 2026, all students who had been assessed were reported to be in stable condition. The Perak State Health Department will continue to monitor the situation, including new cases and laboratory test results, and strengthen control and prevention measures if necessary,” he said in a statement today.
According to him, the school had first brought 57 symptomatic students to a nearby health clinic on Monday, before the figure rose to 61 when an additional 39 symptomatic students were brought in yesterday.
He added that all the students were reported to be in stable condition but at the same time he advised parents and guardians to ensure that symptomatic children do not attend school until they recover.
“Parents are also encouraged to seek health examinations for their children if symptoms persist or worsen, and to consider influenza vaccination through health facilities that provide the service,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sanusi: Too early for seat talks as Kedah PAS, Umno explore political cooperation
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 16 — Kedah PAS and Umno are focusing on creating a positive environment for further discussions on political cooperation, with no requests yet made over seat allocations, Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said.
According to the
New Straits Times
, Sanusi, who is also PAS central election director, said it was still too early for the two parties to discuss the allocation of seats.
“It is still too early to discuss seat allocations. Umno has not asked for anything yet.
“There has been no specific request as we are still at an early stage.
“There will be follow-up discussions later. Once there is a decision at the central level on cooperation between the two parties, we will meet again,” he was quoted as saying.
The
New Straits Times
reported that Sanusi was speaking after receiving a courtesy visit from the Kedah Umno leadership at the Kedah Menteri Besar’s official residence, Seri Mentaloon, yesterday afternoon.
The Umno delegation was led by Kedah Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid and Alor Setar Umno division chief and former Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Bashah Md Hanipah.
PAS was represented by Kedah commissioner and PAS Central Ulama Council chief Datuk Ahmad Yahya, deputy commissioner II Dr Ahmad Fakhruddin Sheikh Fakhrurazi and Kedah secretary Senator Musoddaq Ahmad.
Sanusi stressed that the meeting should not be interpreted as the start of formal cooperation between PAS and Umno in Kedah, describing it instead as an initial step towards creating a more positive environment between the two parties.
“This is not formal cooperation. We need to create a positive environment first. There needs to be a positive environment before we can move on to further discussions.
“This is part of the process. It was a casual discussion, a courtesy visit by Kedah Umno to Kedah PAS and a conversation about the current political scenario,” he was quoted as saying.
Sanusi said the meeting also gave leaders from both parties an opportunity to share their political experiences and discuss Kedah’s future.
He described the gathering as a meeting between experienced political “old hands” who understood the ins and outs of Kedah politics.
“These are people with experience and sufficient understanding who know the ins and outs of Kedah. So, we had a chat.
“I am grateful to all the Umno veterans who visited the official residence of the Menteri Besar.
“We chatted, shared experiences from the past and discussed our expectations for the future,” he was quoted as saying.

Title: Penang air quality hits unhealthy levels statewide, Minden records API of 167
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 16 — Air quality at all four monitoring stations in Penang reached unhealthy levels as of 11am today, with Minden recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 167.
State Housing and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said Balik Pulau recorded an API reading of 164, followed by Seberang Jaya at 162 and Seberang Perai at 160.
He said Minden and Balik Pulau had registered unhealthy readings over the past 24 hours, while readings in Seberang Jaya and Seberang Perai had risen from moderate to unhealthy levels.
“The state government advises the public not to panic but, at the same time, to take precautions, particularly in areas where API readings have reached unhealthy levels,” he said in a statement today.
He advised those with respiratory health problems, children, senior citizens and pregnant women to reduce strenuous or prolonged physical activity outdoors.
“Those experiencing coughing, breathing difficulties, chest discomfort, sore throat or eye irritation should limit their exposure to outdoor air and seek medical advice or treatment if the symptoms persist or worsen,” he said.
Sundarajoo said healthy individuals could continue their daily activities while taking local conditions and the latest API readings into account.
The public was also encouraged to reduce unnecessary outdoor activities should API readings continue to rise.
He said the state government and relevant agencies would continue monitoring air quality and remain in contact with the Department of Environment (DoE) for updated information and assessments.
“The department will step up surveillance of open burning and fires that could contribute to deteriorating air quality, with action to be taken under existing laws where necessary,” he said.
Sundarajoo said industries, particularly those operating in densely populated areas, must cooperate by reducing emissions from major sources.
He reminded the public to avoid activities that contribute to air pollution, including open burning, and to immediately report such incidents to the relevant authorities.

Title: Police: Sri Petaling bomb scare turns out to be team-building game equipment left behind by worker
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks belonging to a company that organises training and team-building programmes, police said today.
Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said police were contacted by a company director, who informed them that the unattended plastic box belonged to his company.
“Investigations found that the box had been left behind by a company employee and contained 20 plastic toy blocks from a game called ‘Radioactive Bomb’, which are used as equipment for group team-building activities.
“Following a team-building programme in Ipoh, Perak, from September 11 to 12, the employee brought the game equipment home but is believed to have accidentally left the box in front of Watsons Sri Petaling while on his way home at about 11pm on September 12,” he told reporters here.
Hoo said the employee had accidentally left the plastic box at the scene due to fatigue after completing the team-building programme.
“Based on the statements obtained, the plastic box and its contents were game equipment belonging to his company and used for team-building activities, with no connection to any criminal activity,” he said.
Hoo added that further checks found the company offers a game called “Radioactive Bomb”, which is designed to encourage cooperation among team members and enhance participants’ mental agility.
“The game is also accompanied by a game module provided by the company in PDF format,” he said.
On September 14, a police bomb disposal unit was called to the scene following a public alert over the discovery.
The box was subsequently destroyed using a bomb disposal device.

Title: MA63 still binding, no ‘new deal’ needed, says Armizan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 16 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) did not cease to exist upon the enactment of the Federal Constitution but remains in force, with the commitments and responsibilities contained therein continuing to be relevant and binding on all parties, said Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said this was in line with Article VIII of MA63, which, among other provisions, requires the governments of the Federation of Malaya, North Borneo and Sarawak to take the necessary legislative, executive or other measures to implement the guarantees, undertakings and recommendations contained in Chapter 3 and Annexes A and B of the Inter-Governmental Committee (IGC) Report.
“This term reaffirms the commitment and responsibility of all parties that agreed to sign the agreement to form the Federation of Malaysia,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with Malaysia Day today.
Armizan said Malaysia, which was formed in 1963, has now reached 63 years, although Sept 16 only became an important date in the official national calendar and was officially celebrated as Malaysia Day from 2010.
He said understanding the history of Malaysia’s formation should not be limited to the Federation of Malaya Agreement 1948, the social contract among the three major ethnic groups or the independence of Malaya in 1957, but must also include full recognition of MA63 as the “birth certificate” of the Federation of Malaysia.
“In conjunction with this 63/63rd anniversary, let us together understand the value and significance of Malaysia Day by embracing the terms of the agreement signed by the nation’s founders, particularly those enshrined in Article VIII of MA63,” he said.
He added that Malaysia did not require a new agreement or what some parties described as a “new deal”, as the provisions of MA63 clearly indicated that the agreement did not expire following the enactment of the Federal Constitution.
“The commitments and responsibilities outlined therein remain relevant and binding — past, present and future,” he said.
Armizan also expressed hope that Malaysia would continue to develop into a stronger and more advanced nation while ensuring prosperity and security for all Malaysians. — Bernama
